_comment: ILLUSTRATIVE — the interface contract the Program Architect would compute from topology.json + requirements.md and pass (as a sibling of `title` in each pipeline child's task.create) so it renders FIRST as the BINDING §6 block. Every leg designs its slice against THESE constants. This is the declarative coordination mechanism (Approach 2). A pipeline child reaching execution without it FAILS LOUD (INTERFACE_CONTRACT_MISSING).

addressing._note: No NAT on this path -> every hop matches the partner CIDR verbatim. This single fact is what makes the interdependency DECLARATIVE (a shared constant) rather than runtime. If a hop introduced source NAT, downstream hops would have to match post-NAT addresses that only exist after that hop's design runs -> Approach 3 (DAG-sequenced).

consistency.noAsymmetricHoles: Every hop permits EXACTLY the endToEndFlow 5-tuple and denies anything broader. Return traffic is the established/related session (stateful) — never a separate broad inbound permit. Node C blocks the program if any leg widens the flow or adds a return-path hole.

perDeviceSlice.edge-fw: untrust -> dmz rule for the flow (+ deny/log). Palo Alto App-ID: allow ssl/web-browsing on 443 or an application-default rule matching the flow.
perDeviceSlice.dmz-sg: aws_security_group.dmz_app ingress from 203.0.113.0/24 tcp/443; egress to 10.20.0.10/32 tcp/443; no 0.0.0.0/0 broadening.
perDeviceSlice.core-fw: dmz -> inside ASA access-list line for the flow (+ explicit deny + log).
